verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我投靠你；求你叫我永不羞愧！
verses.en: In you, O Lord, I have taken shelter.Never let me be humiliated.
verses.commentary:
71:1-6 This opening strophe clearly reveals the mindset of the author. Notice there is no MT
introduction. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1359, suggests that Psalms 70 and 71 may have once been one Psalm.
Most commentators assume this is a prayer of an old man (cf. Ps. 71:9,18) who is being persecuted (cf. Ps. 71:4,10,13,24).

71:1 "I have taken refuge" For this VERB (BDB 340, KB 337, Qal
PERFECT), see notes at Psalm 2:12 and 5:11-12.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

▣ "Let me never be ashamed" This VERB (BDB 101, KB 116) is a
Qal COHORTATIVE used in the sense of a prayer request.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME
(BDB 101, KB 116) IN ITS THEOLOGICAL SENSE

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 求你凭你的公义搭救我，救拔我；侧耳听我，拯救我！
verses.en: Vindicate me by rescuing me.[NOTE:1] Listen to me.[NOTE:2] Deliver me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 71. The psalmist prays for divine intervention and expresses his confidence that God will protect and vindicate him. The first three verses are very similar to Ps 31:1-3a.
Heb “in your vindication rescue me and deliver me.” Ps 31:1 omits “and deliver me.”
Heb “turn toward me your ear.”
verses.commentary:
71:2 There is a series of four prayer requests in this verse (matching the prayer request in v. 1).

- deliver me ‒ BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- rescue me ‒ BDB 812, KB 930, Piel IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- incline Your ear ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- save me ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

Notice the basis of the prayer (i.e., two Hiphil IMPERATIVES,
Ps. 71:2b) is not the psalmist's merits but YHWH's righteousness (cf. Ps. 71:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EFFECTIVE PRAYER

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "Incline Your ear" This VERB (BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) is an anthropomorphic way (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS A HUMAN (anthropomorphic language) to entreat God to hear the psalmist's
prayer (cf. Ps. 17:6; 31:2; 86:1; 88:2; 102:2). The first three verses of this Psalm are similar to Psalm 31:1-3.

verses.zh: 求你作我常住的磐石；你已经命定要救我，因为你是我的岩石，我的山寨。
verses.en: Be my protector and refuge,[NOTE:1] a stronghold where I can be safe.[NOTE:2] For you are my high ridge[NOTE:3] and my stronghold.
notes: Ps 31:2 adds “quickly” before “deliver.”
Heb “become for me a rocky summit of a dwelling place.” The Hebrew term מָעוֹן (maʿon, “dwelling place”) should probably be emended to מָעוֹז (maʿoz, “refuge”; see Ps 31:2).

Heb “to enter, continually you commanded to deliver me.” The Hebrew phrase לָבוֹא תָּמִיד צִוִּיתָ (lavoʾ tamid tsivvita) should be emended to לְבֵית מְצוּדוֹת (levet metsudot, “a house of strongholds”; see Ps 31:2).
verses.commentary:
71:3 "Be to me a rock of habitation" The concept of God as a "high impenetrable
crag" (BDB 700, i.e., fortress, cf. Ps. 71:3c) is seen in Ps. 18:2; 31:2-3; 40:2, which probably
alludes to Deut. 32:31,37.

The concept of "habitation" (BDB 732) denotes a place of dwelling with God
(i.e., the temple, cf. Ps. 76:2), similar to Ps. 23:6; 27:4-6; 90:1; 91:9. The prayer for deliverance
is much more than just the absence of problems or enemies but the very presence of God (cf. Deut. 33:27)!

It is possible that "rock of habitation/dwelling," מעון
could be "rock of refuge," מעוז (BDB 731, cf. Ps. 31:2). The UBS Text
Project (p. 305) gives "dwelling" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The JPSOA translates this as,
"Be a sheltering rock."

▣ "You have given commandment to save me" The VERB (BDB 845,
KB 1010, Piel PERFECT) is translated as

- a past command ‒ NASB, NKJV, NJB, REB

- a future or present request ‒ JPSOA

The UBS Text Project, p. 305, gives "to come always you have commanded" a "C"
rating (i.e., considerable doubt). The NET Bible advocates the UBS's alternate option, "for a fortified
house" (RSV, NRSV), following Psalm 31:2.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，求你救我脱离恶人的手，脱离不义和残暴之人的手。
verses.en: My God, rescue me from the power[NOTE:1] of the wicked,from the hand of the cruel oppressor.
notes: You are my high ridge. This metaphor pictures God as a rocky, relatively inaccessible summit, where one would be able to find protection from enemies. See 1 Sam 23:25, 28.
verses.commentary:
71:4 "Rescue me" In these first four verses several synonyms are used.

- deliver ‒ BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil IMPERFFECT, cf. Ps. 7:1; 39:8;
51:14; 71:11

- rescue ‒ BDB 812, KB 930, Piel IMPERFFECT, Ps. 71:2; Piel
IMPERATIVE, Ps. 71:4, cf. Ps. 18:48; 22:4,8; 31:1; 37:40; 43:1; 82:4; 91:14

- save ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Ps. 71:2; Hiphil
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, Ps. 71:3; used 57 times in the Psalms.

▣ "hand" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "the wicked" See notes at Ps. 1:5; 5:10. Notice the three words used here.

- the wicked ‒ BDB 957, KB 1295

- the wrongdoer ‒ BDB 732, KB 797, Piel ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- ruthless man ‒ BDB 330 III, KB 329, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

It is hard to identify who the wicked enemies are.

verses.zh: 主―耶和华啊，你是我所盼望的；从我年幼，你是我所倚靠的。
verses.en: For you are my hope; O Sovereign Lord, I have trusted in you since I was young.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hand.”
verses.commentary:
71:5-6 Notice the descriptive terms used to characterize "Adonai YHWH" ("my
Lord," cf. Ps. 71:16).

- my hope ‒ BDB 876, cf. Ps. 39:7; 62:5; Jer. 14:8; 17:13

- my confidence ‒ BDB 105 (see note at Isa. 30:10 online)

- my sustainer (lit. I have been supported) ‒ BDB 701, KB 759, Niphal
PERFECT, cf. Isa. 48:2

▣ "from my youth. . .from my birth. . .from my mother's womb" These parallel
phrases are an idiomatic way of asserting the psalmist's confidence that God has always been with him and
for him (cf. Ps. 22:9-10)! These are used of Israel in Isa. 46:3.

This is the worldview of biblical faith as it looks back in time! This causes
continual praise to God (cf. v. 6c).

verses.zh: 我从出母胎被你扶持；使我出母腹的是你。我必常常赞美你！
verses.en: I have leaned on you since birth;[NOTE:1] you pulled me[NOTE:2] from my mother’s womb.I praise you continually.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “O Lord Yahweh, my source of confidence from my youth.”
Heb “from the womb.”

The form in the MT is derived from גָּזָה (gazah, “to cut off”), perhaps picturing God as the one who severed the psalmist’s umbilical cord. Many interpreters and translators prefer to emend the text to גֹחִי (gokhi), from גוּח (gukh) or גִּיח, (gikh, “pull out”; see Ps 22:9; cf. the present translation) or to עוּזִּי (ʿuzzi, “my strength”; cf. NEB “my protector since I left my mother’s womb”).
verses.commentary:
71:6

NASB, NRSV
"took me from"

NKJV
"took me out"

JPSOA
"support"

LXX
"shelter"

TEV
"protected"

The MT has "cut" (BDB 159, KB 186, Qal PARTICIPLE), which
may be figurative of God cutting the umbilical cord (i.e., intimate association with unborn child, like
Ps. 22:9-10; 139:13-16; Jer. 1:5; KB 186).

The other option of "from," "pull," or "strength/support"
(LXX, JPSOA) involves an emendation.

verses.zh: 许多人以我为怪，但你是我坚固的避难所。
verses.en: Many are appalled when they see me,[NOTE:1] but you are my secure shelter.
notes: Heb “in you [is] my praise continually.”
verses.commentary:
71:7-11 This strophe describes the fears of an aged saint. Apparently his aged condition
caused some to question God's presence and care. In Psalms the word "deliver" (BDB 664,
KB 717) is used predominately of God's deliverance.

71:7

NASB
"marvel"

NKJV, Peshitta
"wonder"

NRSV, REB, LXX
"portent"

TEV, JPSOA
"example"

NJB
"bewildered"

The Hebrew word (BDB 68, KB 559) means "a wonder," "a sign," or "a
portent."

- BDB sees its use here as unique, referring to "one protected by YHWH," which would refer to Ps. 71:6.

- KB calls it "portent, in a bad sense."

The fact that two respected Hebrew lexicons come to the opposite understanding in the use of this
root in this context ought to give modern interpreters a pause about just how flexible Hebrew poetry really is!

verses.zh: 你的赞美，你的荣耀终日必满了我的口。
verses.en: I praise you constantlyand speak of your splendor all day long.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like a sign [i.e., portent or bad omen] I am to many.”
verses.commentary:
71:8 This verse parallels the closing line of Ps. 71: 6. This person's life was characterized
by "praise" (BDB 239, cf. Ps. 71:14; Ps. 34:1).

▣ "Your glory" This is not kabod (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [OT]), but another root (BDB 802, KB 1772) which denotes an attribute of
YHWH on HIs creations.

- His person ‒ 1 Chr. 29:11; Ps. 89:17

- His name ‒ 1 Chr. 29:13; Isa. 63:14

- His arm ‒ Isa. 63:12

- His house ‒ Isa. 60:7; 63:15

- His people ‒ Deut. 26:19

This root and kabod are linked in Ps. 96:7-10. He is "beautiful," "radiant," "honorable," and has
"splendor."

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

verses.zh: 我年老的时候，求你不要丢弃我！我力气衰弱的时候，求你不要离弃我！
verses.en: Do not reject me in my old age.[NOTE:1] When my strength fails, do not abandon me.
notes: Heb “my mouth is filled [with] your praise, all the day [with] your splendor.”
verses.commentary:
71:9 Even though this is a person of faith and praise, old age (cf. Eccl. 12:1-7) and the words of
his adversaries had caused him to fear and fret (cf. Ps. 71:18).

This fear is expressed in two IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES.

- do not cast me off ‒ BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 51:11

- do not forsake me ‒ BDB 736, KB 806, Qal IMPERFECT

verses.zh: 我的仇敌议论我；那些窥探要害我命的彼此商议，
verses.en: For my enemies talk about me;those waiting for a chance to kill me plot my demise.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not cast me away at the time of old age.”
verses.commentary:
71:10-11 These verses express what the psalmist's enemies are saying (or at least his perception
of their thoughts).

- God has forsaken him ‒ BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PERFECT (permanent
situation of rejection)

- let us pursue him ‒ BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal IMPERATIVE

- let us seize him ‒ BDB 1074, KB 1779, Qal IMPERATIVE

- for there is no one to deliver him — BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil PARTICIPLE

Psalm 3:2 also describes the evil sayings of those who attack God's faithful followers with doubt.

verses.zh: 说：　神已经离弃他；我们追赶他，捉拿他吧！因为没有人搭救。
verses.en: They say,[NOTE:1] “God has abandoned him.Run and seize him, for there is no one who will rescue him.”
notes: Heb “those who watch for my life consult together.”

verses.zh: 神啊，求你不要远离我！我的　神啊，求你速速帮助我！
verses.en: O God, do not remain far away from me.My God, hurry and help me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “saying.”
verses.commentary:
71:12-16 This strophe has three aspects.

- the psalmist's prayer for, Ps. 71:12

- God's presence (lit. "be not far from me") ‒ BDB 934, KB 1221,
Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense,
cf. Ps. 22:11,19

- God's quick help ‒ BDB 301, KB 300, Qal IMPERATIVE

- the psalmist's prayers for his enemies' demise, Ps. 71:13

- be ashamed ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- be consumed ‒ BDB 477, KB 476, Qal IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- be covered with reproach ‒ BDB 741, KB 813, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- be covered with dishonor ‒ same VERB assumed from c.

- the psalmist's steadfast faith, Ps. 71:14-16

- I will hope continually

- I will praise. . .more and more

- I will tell (i.e., in the temple)

(1) of Your righteousness

(2) of Your salvation

(3) of Your mighty deeds

(4) of Your righteousness, Yours alone

verses.zh: 愿那与我性命为敌的，羞愧被灭；愿那谋害我的，受辱蒙羞。
verses.en: May my accusers be humiliated and defeated.May those who want to harm me[NOTE:1] be covered with scorn and disgrace.
notes: Heb “hurry to my help.”
verses.commentary:
71:13 "adversaries" This is a PARTICIPLE ("the ones accusing,"
BDB 966, KB 1316) of the term often used of Satan, the arch accuser.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

verses.zh: 我却要常常盼望，并要越发赞美你。
verses.en: As for me, I will wait continually,and will continue to praise you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “those who seek my harm.”

verses.zh: 我的口终日要述说你的公义和你的救恩，因我不计其数。
verses.en: I will tell about your justice,and all day long proclaim your salvation,[NOTE:1] though I cannot fathom its full extent.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I add to all your praise.”
Heb “my mouth declares your vindication, all the day your deliverance.”
verses.commentary:
71:15 "My mouth will tell" This VERB (BDB 707, KB 765, Piel
IMPERFECT) is often used in Psalms of proclaiming YHWH's character and deeds in a
worship setting (i.e., temple).

- His wonders ‒ Ps. 9:1; 26:7; 40:5; 75:1; 78:4

- His praise ‒ Ps. 9:14; 79:13; 107:21

- His acts ‒ Ps. 66:16; 118:17; 145:6,12

- His righteousness ‒ Ps. 71:15 (cf. Ps. 35:28; 40:10)

- His covenant love and faithfulness ‒ Ps. 88:11 (cf. Ps. 40:10)

- His glory ‒ Ps. 19:1; 96:3 (cf. Ps. 145:12)

- His greatness ‒ Ps. 145:6

- His Messiah ‒ Ps. 2:7

- His name ‒ Ps. 22:22; 102:21

Here in this verse ‒ His righteousness and His salvation.

▣ "For I do not know the sum of them" This phrase may reflect

- the same truth as Ps. 40:5; 139:18, that God's marvelous acts are too numerous to be
comprehended

- the same truth as Job 42:3; Ps. 139:6, that they are beyond human understanding

- that it means "write" as opposed to "tell" (NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 1288)

verses.zh: 我要来说主―耶和华大能的事；我单要提说你的公义。
verses.en: I will come and tell about[NOTE:1] the mighty acts of the Sovereign Lord.I will proclaim your justice—yours alone.
notes: Heb “though I do not know [the] numbers,” that is, the tally of God’s just and saving acts. HALOT 768 s.v. סְפֹרוֹת understands the plural noun to mean “the art of writing.”

verses.zh: 神啊，自我年幼时，你就教训我；直到如今，我传扬你奇妙的作为。
verses.en: O God, you have taught me since I was young,and I am still declaring[NOTE:1] your amazing deeds.
notes: Heb “I will come with.”
verses.commentary:
71:17-21 This strophe continues the central themes of the psalm. It expresses the
psalmist's declaration of God's character and the certainty of His mercy. Because of this he
will continually tell of God's greatness (i.e., in a temple setting).

71:17a The Israelites were instructed by Moses to teach their children about God
(cf. Exod. 10:12; 12:26; 13:8,14; Deut. 4:9; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 31:13; 32:46). Effective faith
makes the faith of the next generation a priority!

71:17b "wondrous deeds" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL
THINGS (פלא)

verses.zh: 神啊，我到年老发白的时候，求你不要离弃我！等我将你的能力指示下代，将你的大能指示后世的人。
verses.en: Even when I am old and gray,[NOTE:1] O God, do not abandon me,until I tell the next generation about your strengthand those coming after me about your power.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and until now I am declaring.”
Heb “and even unto old age and gray hair.”
verses.commentary:
71:18 Line 1 is a repeat of Ps. 71:9. Notice that the psalmist senses his message about God will
help his generation and generations to come. This is what Scripture is designed to do!

verses.zh: 神啊，你的公义甚高；行过大事的　神啊，谁能像你！
verses.en: Your justice, O God, extends to the skies above;[NOTE:1] you have done great things.[NOTE:2] O God, who can compare to you?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “until I declare your arm to a generation, to everyone who comes your power.” God’s “arm” here is an anthropomorphism that symbolizes his great strength.

Extends to the skies above. Similar statements are made in Pss 36:5 and 57:10.tn Heb “your justice, O God, [is] unto the height.” The Hebrew term מָרוֹם (marom, “height”) is here a title for the sky/heavens.
Heb “you who have done great things.”
verses.commentary:
71:19 "reaches to the heavens" This is an idiom denoting the creative and
redemptive acts of God which are so great and significant they reach the clouds (cf. Ps. 57:10).

▣ "who is like You?" This is a reference to YHWH's uniqueness in a world of
polytheism, henotheism, and animism. This is the essence of Israel's exclusivism!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

verses.zh: 你是叫我们多经历重大急难的，必使我们复活，从地的深处救上来。
verses.en: Though you have allowed me to experience much trouble and distress,[NOTE:1] revive me once again.[NOTE:2] Bring me up once again[NOTE:3] from the depths of the earth.
notes: Or “Who is like you?”
Heb “you who have caused me to see many harmful distresses.”

Heb “you return, you give me life.” The Hebrew term שׁוּב (shuv, “return”) is used here in an adverbial sense, indicating repetition of the action described by the following verb. The imperfects are understood here as expressing the psalmist’s prayer or wish. (Note the use of a distinctly jussive form at the beginning of v. 21.) Another option is to understand this as a statement of confidence, “you will revive me once again” (cf. NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
71:20 This is an admission (in OT terms) of the problems all humans face in this fallen world. The
theology of the "two ways" (cf. Leviticus 26; Deut. 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1) does not explain life
(cf. Psalm 37; 73; and Job).

▣ "revive. . .bring up" These seem to be idioms of restoration to a vigorous
life, not of bodily resurrection. The OT does assert an afterlife (cf. Job 14:14-15; 19:25-27; Dan. 12:2), but
the context here does not hint of this concept. See exegetical notes at Daniel 12 online.

▣ "me" It is possible that the PLURAL "us" should be
in the text. If so, this is another example of a corporate conclusion to an individual Psalm. It would
then parallel Ezekiel 37 (i.e., national revitalization).

▣ "from the depths of the earth" The ancient Israelites buried their people in caves or
graves. Therefore, it is idiomatic to speak of the dead being in the ground. This is imagery for Sheol.
See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD? I. B.

verses.zh: 求你使我越发昌大，又转来安慰我。
verses.en: Raise me to a position of great honor.[NOTE:1] Turn and comfort me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you return, you bring me up.” The Hebrew term שׁוּב (shuv, “return”) is used adverbially to indicate repetition of the action in the next verb. See previous note. If understood as a statement of confidence, it would say, “you will bring me up once again” (cf. NIV, NRSV).

Heb “increase my greatness.” The prefixed verbal form is distinctly jussive, indicating this is a prayer or wish. The psalmist’s request for “greatness” (or “honor”) is not a boastful, self-serving prayer for prominence, but, rather, a request that God would vindicate by elevating him over those who are trying to humiliate him.

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，我要鼓瑟称赞你，称赞你的诚实！以色列的圣者啊，我要弹琴歌颂你！
verses.en: I will express my thanks to you with a stringed instrument,praising[NOTE:1] your faithfulness, O my God.I will sing praises to you accompanied by a harp,O Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfects are understood here as expressing the psalmist’s prayer or wish. (Note the use of a distinctly jussive form at the beginning of v. 21.)
The word “praising” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
71:22-24 The psalmist may have been a Levitical singer (cf. Ps. 71:22). He praises God for
His faithfulness/truth (BDB 54, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: Believe, Trust, Faith, and Faithfulness in the Old Testament ), but
also for the shame and humiliation He brought on his enemies (Ps. 71:24).

71:22 "Holy One of Israel" This is a covenant title for YHWH (cf. Ps. 78:41; 89:18;
so often in Isaiah, i.e., Isa. 1:4; 5:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

verses.zh: 我歌颂你的时候，我的嘴唇和你所赎我的灵魂都必欢呼；
verses.en: My lips will shout for joy. Yes,[NOTE:1] I will sing your praises.I will praise you when you rescue me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The basic sense of the word “holy” is “set apart from that which is commonplace, special, unique.” The Lord’s holiness is first and foremost his transcendent sovereignty as the ruler of the world. He is “set apart” from the world over which he rules. At the same time his holiness encompasses his moral authority, which derives from his royal position. As king he has the right to dictate to his subjects how they are to live; indeed his very own character sets the standard for proper behavior.
Or “when.” The translation assumes that כִּי (ki) has an emphasizing (asseverative) function here.

verses.en: All day long my tongue will also tell about your justice,for those who want to harm me[NOTE:1] will be embarrassed and ashamed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and my life [or “soul”] which you will have redeemed.” The perfect verbal form functions here as a future perfect. The psalmist anticipates praising God, for God will have rescued him by that time.
Heb “those who seek my harm.”

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is this Psalm believed to be written by an older person?

- How is Ps. 71:3 related to Psalm 23:6?

- How is Ps. 71:5-6 related to Jeremiah 1:5?

- Define the word "marvel" in Ps. 71:7.

- Define "ashamed" in Ps. 71:13.

- Does Ps. 71:19c teach monotheism?

- Is Ps. 71:20 referring to healing, restoration of vitality, or resurrection?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.
